paragraphs.source_en: *Samantha:* The MedInfo 2000 eliminates 95 percent of all hospital paperwork because it stores patients’ files electronically. When a nurse administers medication, for example, instead of having to write down the date, time, type of medication, and amount on a patient’s chart, she simply presses a few buttons and it is automatically recorded in an electronic file. Within each hospital, the MedInfo 2000 uses a common network and server so that all of the entries to a patient’s chart are updated automatically. This eliminates the risk of a patient’s getting a double dose of medication, the wrong dose, or not getting his medication at all. The handheld device also offers nurses and doctors instant up-to-date reference material about drug interactions, correct dosage for specific heights and weights, and the latest treatments.
